name: optimize-harness
description: Run a budgeted hill-climbing search over one of PClaw's own artifacts — a template, a skill, an SOP — and file the winner as a proposal. Candidates live in a throwaway sandbox; the live artifact is never written to, and a candidate that touches it is dead regardless of its score.

target_template.help: The PClaw template being optimized — also the results.tsv subject its best-ever score is read back under.

live_target.help: The live artifact's path. This and its .pclaw-lock.json are the FROZEN region: read-only for the whole search.

sandbox.help: A throwaway directory for candidates and the .experience/ index. Must be outside the frozen region — preflight refuses otherwise.

budget_usd.help: The hard dollar ceiling (guardrails SpendMeter). There is no default: an unbudgeted search over model calls has no ceiling at all.

suite_threshold.help: Half one of the dual gate: the harvested regression suite's pass floor. A candidate below it is discarded even when it beats the best-ever.

hypothesis_abandon_after.help: Halt after this many consecutive attempts at the SAME fix — at that point the diagnosis is wrong, not the execution.

no_improvement_halt.help: Halt after this many consecutive iterations whose best score never rose above the window's opening value.

max_iterations.help: The iteration floor under the other three halts — reached only when none of them fires first.

steering_examples.description: Try to improve the code-project template's audit prompt, spend at most two dollars, and show me the best candidate
Stop searching if three candidates in a row fail to beat the current best — do not burn the rest of the budget on a plateau

example_outputs: one template-diff proposal that cleared both the suite threshold and the best-ever score, plus a ledger of every candidate including the discards
no proposal and a named halt reason, when nothing beat the incumbent
metadata.when_not_to_use: not for editing an artifact directly — this only ever proposes, and it costs a model call per candidate. Reach for `refine-template` when one look at a template's run ledger is enough.

children.label: Refuse or report, before the first model call
Propose, scope-check, score, keep or discard

config.prompt:
You are running ONE iteration of a budgeted search over a PClaw artifact. You may only READ and PROPOSE. Your tool set enforces that; do not fight it.

The artifact under optimization:
{{inputs.target_template}}

The LIVE copy, which is frozen:
{{inputs.live_target}}

Your sandbox — the ONLY path you may write to:
{{inputs.sandbox}}

What the preflight measured, including the score you have to beat:
{{nodes.preflight.output}}

What previous iterations of this search already tried is in `{{inputs.sandbox}}/.experience/index.json`, with each candidate's raw diff beside it. Read the diffs, not just the index: the point of keeping them is that the raw prior attempt tells you more than a summary of it.

Method, in order:
  1. Call `refiner_evidence` for the target. Work from its ranked failure clusters, not from a hunch.
  2. Read `.experience/index.json`. A fix whose fingerprint is already there and already failed is not a candidate — repeating it is how a search burns its budget confirming a wrong diagnosis.
  3. Propose ONE candidate edit as typed ops (`update_node` / `insert` / `delete` / `move` / `set_input`). You may NOT touch the artifact's id, name, triggers, or surfacing metadata — those decide WHEN it runs and are frozen.
  4. Write the candidate's diff into your sandbox. Writing anywhere else — above all into {{inputs.live_target}} — is a scope violation, and the adjudicator kills the candidate for it whatever it scored.
  5. Score the candidate against the target's harvested suite and report the number honestly. A score you inflated wins this iteration and loses the search.
  6. Give the fix a stable `fix_fingerprint`: the same string for the same DIAGNOSIS, even when you word the edit differently. That is what lets the search abandon a wrong hypothesis instead of rewording it forever.

Return JSON: {"fix_fingerprint": string, "score": number, "diff_text": string, "rationale": string, "ops": array}

children.label: Diff the frozen region before anything is scored
A frozen-region touch is REFUSED, not merely recorded

config.prompt: This candidate wrote into the frozen region — the live artifact or its .pclaw-lock.json. It is dead regardless of what it scored, and the search must not carry it forward. Approve only if you have personally checked which path it touched and why.

children.label: The dual gate, then the halts
The winner becomes a proposal a human installs

config.prompt:
The search has halted. File its winner — if it has one — as a proposal, and nothing else.

Why it stopped, and the last adjudication:
{{nodes.search.output}}

The candidate ledger, every iteration including the discards:
{{inputs.sandbox}}/.experience/index.json

Do exactly one of these:
  * If the ledger's last `admitted` candidate exists, call `propose_template_diff` with ITS ops, a rationale that cites the score it reached and both halves of the gate it cleared (the suite threshold AND the best-ever), and the halt reason. You are filing a proposal for a person to read and install — you are NOT applying it, and you have no tool that could.
  * If nothing was admitted, propose NOTHING and say so. A search that found no improvement has produced a result, not a failure; inventing a proposal to have something to show is the one outcome worse than an empty one.

Never file a candidate whose outcome was `scope_violation`. It touched the frozen region, which makes it dead regardless of what it scored.

Return JSON: {"proposed": boolean, "halt_reason": string, "winner_score": number, "rationale": string, "proposal_id": string}
